item.title: Starting my doctorate at the University of Bonn
item.description:
In October 2026 I started my doctorate — a Doctor of Agricultural Sciences (Dr. agr.) at the University of Bonn, supervised by Prof. Dr. Frank Ewert. The research itself is carried out at the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) in Müncheberg, Germany.

Research focus

Landscape-scale agroecosystem modelling: spatial and temporal landscape dynamics, crop productivity and resilience.

The question I am working on

How can spatial and temporal landscape information be represented and integrated into agroecosystem models to improve the understanding and prediction of crop productivity and resilience across scales?

I will share updates, code and results here as the project develops.

item.title: Moderating the Hy4Cast workshop at Tropentag 2025
item.description: At Tropentag 2025, hosted by the University of Bonn, I moderated the workshop “Hy4Cast – Hybrid modelling leveraging Artificial Intelligence for fine-scale crop yield forecasts”.

item.title: Two posters at EGU 2025
item.description:
At the EGU General Assembly 2025 in Vienna I presented two posters:

  • Transforming Low-Resolution CORINE Data into High-Resolution Landscape Maps with Semi-Supervised Deep Learning
  • Advancing Crop Yield Predictions: The Potential of Diffusion Models in Machine Learning for Agriculture

Both are listed on my presentations page.

item.title: Joining ZALF as a Research Scientist
item.description:
In January 2025 I joined the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) in Müncheberg, Germany, as a Research Scientist. I work in the Research Platform Simulation and Data Science, in the Working Group Multi-Scale Modelling and Forecasting (MSM), and contribute to the Leibniz-Lab Systemic Sustainability (LL SYSTAIN) project.

My work there covers:

  • machine learning workflows for multi-scale crop yield forecasting and scenario analysis, integrating climate, soil and biodiversity indicators;
  • processing and harmonising large Earth observation and agricultural datasets (Sentinel, MODIS, soil grids);
  • co-designing sustainability indicators that link agricultural productivity and ecological resilience, together with interdisciplinary teams.
